title: Python SDK: schema-evolution shims and example patterns
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a compact set of compatibility shims, examples, and migration guidance for schema evolution in the Python SDK. Focus areas: (1) stable typed model factories that tolerate optional/unknown fields, (2) streaming response adapters that can skip/ignore new fields without breaking, and (3) easy-to-reason idempotent retry constructors for partial/fragmented stream reassembly.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a lightweight 'SchemaShim' helper that can map old response shapes to new dataclass/Pydantic models without runtime schema hacks
Ship three example notebooks showing: (a) model with added optional fields, (b) field renamed via mapping shim, (c) streaming fragment reassemble with idempotent retry
Add unit + property tests that simulate forwards/backwards incompatible payloads and validate graceful degradation
Documentation page in docs/sdk/python/schema-evolution with migration recipes and code samples
Land a draft PR that includes the shim helpers and one example consumer app
design_notes: Prefer composition over inheritance for shim behaviors to keep runtime overhead minimal
Use dataclass + typing.Annotated metadata to declare alternate field names and deprecation hints
Streaming adapters should operate on event-level JSON dicts and emit hydrated models when enough info is available
Retry constructor: provide deterministic idempotency token generation and checkpointable stream cursors
Avoid adding global opt-outs; prefer explicit per-route opt-in for lenient parsing to reduce silent data-loss risks
